chunks: Our father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah quoted Ya'qub ibn Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Murazim ibn Hakim al-Azdi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
God's Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) taught Ali (peace be upon him) one thousand gates, each of which opens up to another one thousand gates.

key_terms.صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ: peace be upon him and his family

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the 'one thousand gates' of knowledge taught to Imam Ali in this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to illustrate the depth of Imam Ali’s prophetic inheritance, often interpreted by Shia scholars as encompassing both exoteric jurisprudence and esoteric gnosis (‘ilm al-batin). The metaphor of 'one thousand gates, each opening to a thousand' signifies the infinite, layered nature of divine wisdom accessible through the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing their role as the sole legitimate interpreters of the Quran. This concept underscores the Shia belief that the Prophet’s knowledge was not merely transmitted but fully actualized in Ali, making him the gate (Bab) to the Prophet’s inner truth.
